application_review: RoughHorizontalError proves integer scaling of the standard mod-one norm, removal of finite integer parts, conversion from either sample step 1 or t to the rough step t, the scaled higher-term error bound for p<=Z, and one finite descending coefficient estimate.

RoughHorizontalInterpolation combines that coefficient estimate with the exact interpolation theorem. Its eventual threshold precedes all t,m,theta, all pointwise choices p(z) in {1,t+mz}, and all higher coefficient values and integer approximations. The output is an actual smooth-denominator rational polynomial, integral at every original index, with explicit H-independent error constant.

RoughBinomialWeights proves the actual finite product binomial weight bound <=2^D*p^(degreeJ-degreeI), strict degree increase for distinct comparable multiindices, and the original multiindex obstruction estimate with constant A0+card(s)*2^D*A.

Compared with Section 06 lines 378-436. The proof removes actual integer combinations in the circle norm, then controls their real errors; it does not assume that small mod-one error is small real error.

Integer scaling is valid for every integer, including negative integers, with its absolute real value. The sample step conversion treats p=1 and p=t separately and gives the explicit factor 2^e from t<=2S.

The higher-term bound explicitly requires p<=Z. The interpolation wrapper derives 2S<=Z eventually from PowerDominates and proves every permitted p(z)<=2S. No unproved uniform asymptotic estimate is inserted.

The binomial weight is the actual product of natural binomial coefficients and natural residue powers; the degree difference identity requires componentwise I<=J. Distinct comparable indices have strictly larger total degree. The bound only depends on the degree cap D and higher-term count, not progression length H or polynomial coefficients.

The generic interpolation step accepts higher integer approximations with error exponent e+n(i). The multiindex estimate proves this matches total degree J using n=degreeJ-degreeI. All p(z) choices may vary separately at each index.

This batch proves a single induction step and the needed numerical weights, not a completed simultaneous descending induction, a substituted-polynomial coefficient identity, or a quantitative Leibman obstruction. Those remain explicit obligations.
All retained proof sources and axiom sets are unchanged. These are author-side checks, not independent kernel replay.
